## What's new

Threadnote 5.3.5 keeps recall responsive by serving ready indexed data while maintenance continues safely in the background.

### Recall without avoidable waits

`threadnote recall` and MCP recall now read a ready local snapshot while automatic synchronization and index maintenance continue in the background. Foreground recall waits for validated data, a real failure, or cancellation from its caller instead of stopping at an internal timeout.

### Confirm lexical and vector recall preparation

`threadnote repair` and `threadnote index rebuild` now wait for lexical and vector recall indexes to be ready for the inputs they inspected. They report source, model, or authorization drift rather than presenting outdated recall readiness as current.

### See the next workflow task

Use `threadnote workflow task-view --run-id <id> --caller-cwd <path>` or the `workflow_task_view` MCP tool to read the next actionable task for an existing native workflow run, with optional implementation, review, or delivery role filtering.

### Safer workflow handoffs

Native workflow cycles preserve source evidence when an ordinary merge updates their base. Review follow-ups now keep shared feature knowledge current without duplicate publication requests, so task and review history stays connected to the source that actually shipped.

### Clearer Manager availability

Manager now explains when a ready recall snapshot is temporarily unavailable and directs you to retry after background maintenance or run `threadnote repair`.

### More flexible development plans

Development plans can describe an architecture clearly in prose when a diagram would not add useful understanding.
